mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant negative trend (t-test p > 0.05) following a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant negative trend (t-test p > 0.05) following a 0.5% increase in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant negative trend (t-test p > 0.05) following two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant positive trend (t-test p > 0.05) following a 1% increase in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, indicating higher inflation, and the federal funds rate is below 1%, the S&P 500 forward returns tend to be negative over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and monetary policy is expected to tighten.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 1%
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with low interest rates
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant negative trend (t-test p > 0.05) following the described interaction of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100k in 1 month and UNRATE increases > 0.3%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant negative trend (t-test p > 0.05) following the described interaction of PAYEMS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two months signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased construction activity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant positive trend (t-test p > 0.05) following a 5% increase in HOUST over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending, a major component of GDP, declines.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant negative trend (t-test p > 0.05) following a 1% decrease in RSAFS.
